plan: OpenVibe End-to-End Realignment & Implementation Plan, revision 3 (20 Sep 2026)
runtime: node 22, express, PostgreSQL 18 (openvibe-sdk/db, async) + Valkey 9, ffmpeg
pastes: OpenVibe.Community is the paste authority since 2026-09-22 (PASTES_MOVED_TO); Media's paste API is read-only and every write answers 410 pastes.moved, /p/:slug 301s to Community and Media serves screenshot bytes only (the read-only API is being retired, T10 step 2)
deployment: Public at https://openvibe.media: deployed with `sudo ovhost deploy media` (restart refused while a VOD records; --wait-idle), /opt/openvibe.media, unit openvibe-media on 127.0.0.1:4100 behind the openvibe.media nginx vhost, principal media.
features: VOD recording (RTMP pull, RTP ingest), chunk ingest and finalize
storage tiering local, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2 with copy verification and a disk guardian
canonical object model (/api/v2) with namespaces, holds, derivatives and lifecycle
media jobs with leases, retries and proposals
multi-tenant apps and developer-project tenants (sandbox separated)
public serving with presigned URLs; signed access for private and sandbox items
the object explorer (/me) and operator views
media.* events through the SDK outbox, webhooks during the transition
restore-drill mode and N-1 compatibility tests
placement demand rollups on Valkey (F2.4): reads per object × region × 5-minute bucket, hotness over the hour, media.object.hot once per object per hour

tiering on demand (F2.5): the object sweep promotes and demotes on the hour's Valkey reads against per-class hysteresis bands, one MGET per page, falling back to the daily PostgreSQL counts for a whole sweep when Valkey fails

placement constraints (F2.6): sweep moves refused while their provider fails its class (breaker or probe), and a per-class monthly R2 storage ceiling (maxHotUsdPerMonth) applied in value order, each explained in the decision's inputs

every storage class in the native-object sweep: kind and mime type classify video/image/download, an app may declare game-asset/attachment/backup (or any of the six) in the object's metadata (metadata.class, or media_class/placement_class), and each class spends its own per-sweep budget, hysteresis band and R2 storage ceiling

segment-native video (F3.1, behind MEDIA_HLS_ENABLED): the media_timeline index, the object.cmaf job (CMAF/fMP4 segments of a finished video on its own keyframes, sha256 and durability per row, idempotent) and HLS playlists written from the timeline at /o/:id/master.m3u8 under the object's access checks

packing after finalize (F3.3, behind MEDIA_HLS_ENABLED): the object.pack job concatenates durable segments into ~60 s chunk objects verified by sha256, each media_timeline row naming its byte range; the segment route serves a packed segment as a ranged read of its chunk; the per-segment keys are deleted once the chunk is durable; segment providers come from the placement router; a finished object.cmaf queues object.pack by itself (dedupeActive: a rerun joins an active pack, a later cut queues a new one)

timeline sprites (F3.1, behind MEDIA_HLS_ENABLED): object.sprite cuts its sheet from the object's media_timeline rows — each sample time picks the row covering it and one frame is decoded from that row's bytes (this node's segment, or a packed row's byte range in its chunk), checked against the row's sha256 — with the same layout and metadata as the seek path, so a packed long VOD is never decoded end to end; a source without a timeline keeps one fast seek per frame

HLS discovery on the v1 shapes (F3.c, behind MEDIA_HLS_ENABLED): the VOD and clip answers (vodPublic/clipPublic — get, list, create, update) carry hls_url (and hls_expires_at when the object is private or sandbox), the same field and access rules as GET /o/:id/download?format=json, read through one shared discovery (server/objects/hls.js); an object without a timeline gets object.cmaf queued and the field appears once it ran, and a virtual clip plays its source's window without being cut a timeline of its own
